edges.description: Deficient central myelination underlies the severe motor arrest and global developmental delay.
Early nystagmus reflects involvement of myelinated oculomotor pathways.
Dystonia accompanies the central white-matter and associated grey-matter involvement.

edges.limitations: Non-neural cells for the biochemistry; the neuronal line is a cancer-derived model.
Transient morpholino knockdown at the larval stage only; morpholino phenotypes are not always reproduced in stable mutants.
Invertebrate glia with no vertebrate myelin.

nodes.description: Homozygous or compound heterozygous germline DEGS1 variants (missense, nonsense, frameshift, splice, and whole- or partial-gene deletions). Most variants abolish activity in vitro and lower protein levels by 40-80%; N255S and L175Q keep about 12% of wild-type activity.

evidence.reference_title: Loss of the sphingolipid desaturase DEGS1 causes hypomyelinating leukodystrophy.
evidence.snippet: we have used whole-exome sequencing in patients with undetermined leukoencephalopathies to uncover the endoplasmic reticulum lipid desaturase DEGS1 as the causative gene in 19 patients from 13 unrelated families

evidence.reference_title: Loss of function and reduced levels of sphingolipid desaturase DEGS1 variants are both relevant in disease mechanism.
evidence.snippet: We conclude that loss of function and reduced protein levels are both relevant in disease pathogenesis

nodes.description: Diffuse deficiency of central myelin, seen on MRI as hypomyelination with a thin corpus callosum; serial imaging in some patients shows partial improvement, consistent with hypomyelination rather than strict demyelination.

nodes.description: CRISPR DEGS1-knockout HEK-293T and HAP1 cells, patient fibroblasts, and SH-SY5Y cells carrying the H132R leukodystrophy variant.

evidence.reference_title: DEGS1-associated aberrant sphingolipid metabolism impairs nervous system function in humans.
evidence.snippet: a patient with a multisystem neurological disorder of both the central and peripheral nervous systems

nodes.description: Dihydroceramide and other dihydrosphingolipids build up, with a raised dihydroceramide/ceramide ratio, in patient fibroblasts, muscle and blood. Karsai found dihydro species made up about 40% of plasma sphingolipids against about 10% in controls.

evidence.reference_title: DEGS1-associated aberrant sphingolipid metabolism impairs nervous system function in humans.
evidence.snippet: The blood sphingolipid profile in the patient showed a significant increase in dihydro sphingolipid species that was further recapitulated in patient-derived fibroblasts, in CRISPR/Cas9-derived DEGS1-knockout cells, and by pharmacological inhibition of DEGS1.

nodes.description: Loss of the DEGS1 homolog ifc gives dihydroceramide accumulation, glial ER expansion, lipid-droplet loss, failed neuronal ensheathment and neuronal death; schlank knockdown rescues the ER phenotype.

evidence.reference_title: Loss of the sphingolipid desaturase DEGS1 causes hypomyelinating leukodystrophy.
evidence.snippet: severe motor arrest, early nystagmus, dystonia, spasticity, and profound failure to thrive

nodes.description: Ceramide-synthase inhibition one step upstream of DEGS1 lowers the dihydroceramide/ceramide imbalance. In zebrafish, fingolimod reduced the ratio, improved locomotion and increased myelinating oligodendrocytes. There is no human trial.

evidence.reference_title: Loss of the sphingolipid desaturase DEGS1 causes hypomyelinating leukodystrophy.
evidence.snippet: The enzymatic inhibition of Cer synthase by fingolimod, 1 step prior to DEGS1 in the pathway, reduced the critical DhCer/Cer imbalance and the severe locomotor disability, increasing the number of myelinating oligodendrocytes in a zebrafish model.

nodes.description: In the absence of Delta-4 desaturation, an atypical sphingoid base with the double bond at position 14 instead of 4 is formed. It is a specific biomarker that discriminates pathogenic from benign DEGS1 variants; whether it is itself neurotoxic in vivo is not established (see discussion).
nodes.id: Formation of Atypical Sphingoid Base SPB 18:1(14Z)

evidence.reference_title: The atypical sphingolipid SPB 18:1(14Z);O2 is a biomarker for DEGS1 related hypomyelinating leukodystrophy.
evidence.snippet: the SPB 18:1(14Z);O2 seems to be a more specific biomarker to discriminate between pathogenic and benign DEGS1 variants

nodes.description: In Drosophila glia, loss of the DEGS1 homolog ifc causes ER expansion, lipid-droplet loss and failure to ensheath neurons. ifc is expressed mainly in glia. Mapping fly ensheathment onto vertebrate myelination is a proxy.

evidence.reference_title: Loss of dihydroceramide desaturase drives neurodegeneration by disrupting endoplasmic reticulum and lipid droplet homeostasis in glial cells.
evidence.snippet: Loss of ifc causes massive dihydroceramide accumulation and severe morphological defects in cortex glia, including endoplasmic reticulum (ER) expansion, failure of neuronal ensheathment, and lipid droplet depletion.

evidence.snippet: The enzymatic activity in patient fibroblasts was reduced by 80% compared with wild-type cells, which was in line with a reduced expression of mutant DEGS1 protein.

nodes.description: DEGS1 is a MAM-resident enzyme, and its loss gives a hyperfused mitochondrial network, impaired sterol O-acyltransferase activity with fewer cholesteryl esters, abnormal lipid-droplet biogenesis, and more mitochondrial superoxide, shown in patient fibroblasts and muscle. Its link to myelin failure is an inference.

evidence.reference_title: Sphingolipid desaturase DEGS1 is essential for mitochondria-associated membrane integrity.
evidence.snippet: a hyperfused mitochondrial network associated with decreased activation of dynamin-related protein 1

nodes.description: Progressive loss of neural tissue, seen clinically as progressive thalamic and cerebellar atrophy. The fly model places this downstream of glial dysfunction.

evidence.reference_title: Loss of dihydroceramide desaturase drives neurodegeneration by disrupting endoplasmic reticulum and lipid droplet homeostasis in glial cells.
evidence.snippet: Reduction of DEGS1 dihydroceramide desaturase function causes pediatric neurodegenerative disorder hypomyelinating leukodystrophy-18 (HLD-18).

nodes.description: Dihydroceramide accumulation mislocalises active Rac1 and drives Rac1-NADPH-oxidase-dependent reactive oxygen species, causing neurodegeneration in Drosophila photoreceptors and in SH-SY5Y cells carrying the leukodystrophy DEGS1 H132R variant; suppressing Rac1-NOX rescues it.

evidence.reference_title: Dihydroceramide desaturase regulates the compartmentalization of Rac1 for neuronal oxidative stress.
evidence.snippet: DEGS1/ifc deficiency causes dihydroceramide accumulation, resulting in Rac1 mislocalization and NOX-dependent neurodegeneration.
